title: chore: resync framework workflow to aidevops canonical caller
body:
## Summary

Resync `.github/workflows/issue-triage-gate.yml` to the canonical aidevops caller template
(reusable-workflow pattern, GH#20649 + GH#20727).

**Classification before**: `NO-WORKFLOW`
**Ref**: `@main`

## Why

The aidevops framework ships managed GitHub Actions workflows as reusable
workflows. Downstream repos carry ~45-line callers that delegate all logic
to the configured aidevops reusable workflow repository/ref.

This PR brings this repo in line with the canonical template, eliminating
drift and unblocking automatic updates when the framework evolves.

## How to verify

After merge, trigger an event matching the workflow triggers. Framework
scripts are fetched at runtime via a secondary checkout — no
`.agents/scripts/` files are needed in this repo.

## Rollback

If the workflow breaks, revert this PR. The previous workflow is preserved
in git history at the parent commit.

Generated by: `aidevops sync-workflows --apply` (see marcusquinn/aidevops#20649).

## Later deployment sequence

This PR does not deploy or change Cloudflare. When the client Graph app is ready:

1. Set the four Worker secrets and the documented `LEAD_RATE_LIMIT` binding.
2. Upload the Worker with the guarded deployment helper.
3. Chris sends the first live test submission and confirms delivery and Sent Items.

title: GH#17: Technical SEO for the BCT homepage
body:
For #17

## Summary

- Scope the title, description, production canonical and social metadata to `/`, the only indexable HTML route on `main`. Open Graph and Twitter use the existing 1920×1080 earthwork image.
- Replace the previous structured data with a linked `Organization` and `WebSite` graph. No address, telephone, geo, or unverified social profiles.
- Describe all seven homepage images. Use 2026-11-25, the date of the latest homepage content change, for sitemap `lastmod` rather than the build time. Visible copy and PR #12 are unchanged.

## Runtime Testing (runtime-verified)

- `npm run build` (Next.js 16.3.6), `npm run lint -- --max-warnings=0`, and `npm run test:worker` (4 tests) passed.
- `next start` + `curl` verified a single title (47 characters), description (148 characters), canonical, matching Open Graph and Twitter image URLs, and descriptive alt text on all seven images.
- `curl` verified the sole canonical URL and its `lastmod` in `/sitemap.xml`, and verified that `/robots.txt` allows `/` and points to the sitemap.
- The Schema.org validator reported no issues on the rendered homepage.
